conclusions.result: The temporary .mjs wrapper preserves the intended delay, real readiness and cleanup checks while allowing appended Codex -c arguments to remain script arguments. It removes Node eval/check parsing incompatibility without timeout increases or retries.

The fixture now supplies consistent provider identity in thread, session, defaults and catalog. Tuple selection and submitted modelProvider/model/effort remain asserted. The current picker and executionOptions preserve exact same-provider model and supported effort; stale or incompatible settings are rejected.

Added native assertions require no parent/fork link, new session ID/header identity, no history_base, and distinct path/inode. Existing original deletion, process restart and continuation proof remains. UI conversion submits no draft input; accepted handoff requires a distinct target and current navigation/draft ownership. Unknown receipt queries do not replay conversion.
Exact argv expectations now include the fixed native override. Original escaping and descendant/owner-death/backpressure/cleanup assertions remain; production controller logic is unchanged.

Relevant accepted/unknown mutations and thread events refresh the sidebar without changing selection. Project invalidation is synchronous; refresh cleanup is scope-bound. Pending or unknown conversion and active conversion busy state block automatic source resume; scoped handoff preserves the source draft and does not steal a later user navigation.

The two docs require retained complete failure evidence, distinction between product/fixture/environment causes, missed-check analysis, analogous-consumer inspection, concrete prevention and honest remaining limits. The CI1 table matches the retained failed run and does not claim Linux success or zero coverage gaps. Existing audit authorization remains required.
